language.script_notes: Street suffixes: Calle, Avenida, Carrera, Transversal, Diagonal, Autopista — the Carrera/Calle grid-numbering system used in Colombian cities is a distinctive national convention.

road_furniture.guardrail_type: Standard steel guardrail, common on mountainous Andean roads given the terrain.
road_furniture.line_paint: White outside/yellow inside is common, with yellow outside/white inside also seen.
road_furniture.curb_style: Painted kerbs in cities; narrow, winding mountain roads common in the Andean interior.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Distinctively narrow pole-mounted signs. Terpel, EcoPetrol, Puma, Esso, Texaco and Biomax are common fuel-station brands.

architecture.roof_style: Varies sharply by region — colonial tile roofs on the coast and in Andean colonial towns, corrugated metal common in warmer lowland areas. See regional profiles.
architecture.wall_construction: Highly regional — colourful Spanish colonial architecture on the Caribbean coast (Cartagena), dense modern high-rise development in Bogotá/Medellín, traditional coffee-region farmhouses in the Andean interior.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: UNESCO-listed colonial Cartagena old town; modern high-rise Bogotá/Medellín skylines set against Andean mountain backdrops; traditional wooden coffee-farm houses (fincas) in the Eje Cafetero.

nature.vegetation: Extremely varied — tropical Caribbean coastal vegetation in the north, cool high-altitude Andean cloud forest and coffee plantations in the interior, treeless savanna grassland in the Llanos, and dense Amazon rainforest in the south. See regional profiles.
nature.terrain: The Andes split into three parallel mountain ranges (cordilleras) running through the country's center; a Caribbean coast in the north, a Pacific coast in the west, and vast eastern lowlands (Llanos savanna transitioning to Amazon rainforest) making up roughly half the country's area.
nature.climate_signature: No single national climate — hot and humid on both coasts, cool and temperate in the high Andean cities (Bogotá sits at ~2,600m), hot and wet in the Amazon and Llanos.

vehicles.plate_color: Yellow plates with black text — a strong, reliable national tell.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Willys Jeeps (a Colombian coffee-region cultural icon, especially in the Eje Cafetero) and colourful 'chiva' rural buses are notable regional tells.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mixed Gen 3/4 official coverage concentrated in major cities, supplemented by Trekker imagery elsewhere.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Dense around Bogotá, Medellín and Cartagena; sparse in the Llanos and Amazon regions.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Andean/Caribbean coast geography and Llanos savanna straddling the border
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Colombia's yellow license plates and distinctive narrow pole signage differ from Venezuela's road furniture; Venezuela has had far less Street View updating in recent years, so coverage age/quality can also be a tell.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Andean mountain terrain and similar coffee-growing highland agriculture
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Colombia's Carrera/Calle grid street-naming convention and yellow plates differ from Ecuador's road furniture and signage.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shares a border and some similar tropical coastal architecture/vegetation near the Caribbean
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Panama's plates and road signage differ from Colombia's; Panama also has a notably different urban skyline (Panama City) and the Panama Canal as a unique landmark.
